property_summary: For any deployed contract C the public owner() getter returns exactly the stored owner address; the mutant offsets the stored owner by +1 so owner() will differ for some owner values (e.g. when stored owner != address(uint160(address)+1)).

For any deployed C the public owner() getter returns exactly the stored owner address; the mutant shifts the returned address by +1 (casting to uint160 and adding 1), so there exists some stored owner for which owner() differs — the test fuzzes stored owner by calling initialize from an arbitrary caller and checks owner() equals the initializer address.

For any initializer caller address A, after initialize(...) the contract's owner() returns exactly A (the initializer); the mutant that returns owner()+1 will therefore differ for some initializer addresses and cause the property to fail.

After calling initialize(...) from any non-zero caller, owner() should return the exact address that initialized the contract; the mutant offsets the returned owner by +1 (as uint160), breaking equality for some initializer addresses.

After initialize(...) is called by any non-zero EOA, owner() must return that initializer address for all admissible inputs; the mutant adds 1 to the stored owner when returning, causing owner() to differ for at least some initializer addresses.

For any deployed contract C, paused() returns the actual stored paused state (i.e., paused() == c.paused() should reflect the internal _paused flag: when not paused the function returns false and when paused it returns true); the mutant flips the boolean so for some inputs (after calling pause or unPause) paused() will return the opposite, causing the property to fail.

For any sequence of calls, the public paused() view returns the actual paused state (true iff contract is paused); the mutant flips this boolean so paused() disagrees with the stored paused state for some inputs.
